text:
Theo’s obsession with the night sky was not merely a pastime but a sacred ritual inherited from his mother, Dr. Elena Vance, a brilliant astrophysicist who taught him that the universe was a language waiting to be understood. After her sudden passing when he was ten, the rooftop became his sanctuary, a place where he felt closest to her voice in the whisper of the wind. He believed that if he could just map every star perfectly, he might find a signal she left behind. This deep-seated need for connection drove his meticulous nature and his reluctance to leave the quiet of his rural home, as the open sky was the only place where he felt truly heard.

One evening, as Theo adjusted his telescope, he noticed an unusual formation of clouds gathering above the horizon. He remembered his mother’s playful explanation that fluffy things in the sky rain comes from, a whimsical notion she used to make the complex physics of precipitation accessible to a young child. While scientists explained condensation and droplets, Theo held onto the magic of those soft, white shapes, seeing them not just as weather patterns but as gentle reminders of the cycles of life and loss. As the first drops began to fall, washing the dust from the stars, Theo felt a strange sense of peace, realizing that just as the rain nourished the earth, his memories of his mother continued to sustain him, even in the darkest nights.
